prompt: Repaint this rock pillar as a different, wilder crag of the same stone. Keep how it is painted: one single solid block of stone with big flat broken facets and sharp edges, the same three-quarter view from slightly above so the top and two side faces show, the same flat grey ink wash and dark brush outline, the same plain empty aged-paper background. Change its shape: make it lean a little to one side, broad and heavy at its flat base and narrowing upward, about twice as tall as it is wide, and break its top into two unequal jagged peaks, one clearly taller than the other, with a deep V-shaped notch between them. Give its outline big irregular steps and overhanging broken corners so that no edge is straight from bottom to top. Two or three deep vertical cracks. It stays one solid block: no stacked slabs, no thin plates or sheets, no nested outlines, no horizontal bands, no small blocks around the foot, no small marks or dots around the edge. Whole rock in frame with a paper margin all round, no shadow.
